subject: Acme: follow-up on SDK/auth + request/response schema questions
thread_summary: Post-discovery follow-up covering SDK setup, auth options, chat vs completions semantics, tokenization/max_tokens/stop behavior, streaming, and embedding/reranker guidance. Schedule SE deep-dive and share quickstart materials.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Acme: follow-up on SDK/auth + request/response schema questions

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

- Goal: add contextual LLM features to Acme's support flow (ticket summarization + reranking knowledge hits + structured troubleshooting actions).
- Primary constraints: < 300ms p95 production latency for simple completions, private VPC deployment preferred for PHI, and strict tokenization accounting for billing.

Immediate asks we discussed that I wanted to follow up on:
1) SDK setup & auth: are you planning to use server-side API keys (backend) or client-based auth (embedded tools / mobile)? Any org policy re: OAuth/KMS?
2) Routing & deployment: would you want Hosted API first or go straight to Private (VPC)?
3) Request/response schema: for the structured actions we discussed, do you prefer function/tool-calling (strongly-typed JSON responses) or parsing completions with stop/newline heuristics?
4) Tokenization & max_tokens: do you have hard caps on output tokens per response? We should align on truncation and stop token behavior.

Next steps I propose:
- Share a short tech note (attached) with SDK quickstart and examples for chat vs completions + streaming semantics.
- Schedule a 60-min SE call (Vivek) to walk architecture and run through sample requests (auth flows, embeddings + reranker pipeline).

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (quick examples for chat/completions/embeddings)

If you can reply with answers to the bullets above and a couple of available windows (TZ: PST), we'll lock the SE call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>

Date: 2026-03-21T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: follow-up on SDK/auth + request/response schema questions

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick answers from our side:

- Auth: we'll be using server-side requests from our backend services (no client-side keys). We prefer API-key-based flows initially; long-term we may integrate with our internal KMS for rotating keys.
- Deployment: prefer Hosted for an initial POC, but must evaluate Private/VPC for production because of PHI.
- Structured responses: we like the function/tool-calling idea for actions (more robust than trying to parse freeform).
- Token limits: for summarization we'd like outputs capped at ~400 tokens; for short actions, < 100 tokens. Important that stop sequences are respected — sometimes we have nested JSONs and need clean cutoffs.

Also: we use chunked streaming on our endpoints for other vendors; streaming is preferred to render incremental UI, but we need clarity on how Redwood signals partial vs final tokens and how truncated responses are indicated.

Available windows for SE call: Mon 3/23 10–11am PST or Tue 3/24 1–2pm PST.

I'll attach our rough network diagram to help with the deployment discussion.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Acme: follow-up on SDK/auth + request/response schema questions

Hi Samir / team — quick technical notes ahead of our call to save time. TL;DR: chat vs completions is about conversational context and structured turn-taking; function/tool-calling is the recommended approach for deterministic JSON outputs; streaming and token accounting behave as outlined below.

1) Chat vs Completions\- Chat: preserves role-based message history (system/user/assistant). Good for multi-turn with context window management.\- Completions: single prompt -> continuation; simpler for one-shot prompts. Use chat API when you need conversational state and instruction anchoring.

2) Function / tool calling for structured output\- We provide a function-calling schema where you declare expected JSON schema (types/required fields). The model will attempt to emit JSON conforming to the schema. If the model emits invalid JSON, the SDK has a validate+repair helper (best-effort). This pattern is more reliable than freeform parses + stop sequences for nested JSON.

3) Tokenization & max_tokens\- Token counts align with standard BPE tokenizers (we use the model tokenizer; tokenization examples in the quickstart).\- max_tokens controls the maximum number of output tokens the model will generate. If output hits the limit, generation is truncated and we surface a 'truncated' flag in the response metadata. Important: when using function-calling, allow a buffer for closing braces / metadata.

4) Stop sequences\- Stop sequences are honored by the decoder; if multiple stop sequences are present, the earliest is applied. For structured outputs, stop sequences are risky when the model may emit internal punctuation — function-calling is safer.

5) Streaming semantics\- We stream token deltas as they're decoded. Each streamed event includes:
  - tokens: incremental text tokens (string)
  - is_final: boolean-like indicator sent in the final event
  - truncated: boolean-like indicator if generation ended due to max_tokens

Note: since you prefer server-side API keys, the SDK supports chunked streaming over HTTP/2 and Websockets. We'll demo both.

6) Embeddings + reranker pattern\- Typical pattern: embed query and candidate docs, compute FAISS/ANN similarity to narrow candidates, then re-rank top-K candidates with a cross-encoder (we provide a light-weight reranker sample that uses embeddings + contextual rerank prompts). Embeddings calls are independent endpoints (vector outputs) and are billed separately.

References: https://docs.redwood.ai/api#chat-vs-completions and the quickstart PDF Marissa attached.

I'll cover code samples and live requests in the call. See you Monday 10am PST.

—Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick clarifications before the call:

- On the truncated flag: will that be in the JSON response envelope even for streamed responses? We need a reliable hook client-side to show "response cut short" in the UI.
- For function-calling, can we pass a strict JSON schema (e.g., JSON Schema draft-07) or is it simplified? We have nested objects in our action payloads.

Otherwise Monday works. Looking forward to the demo.

Samir
